name: Kiro

surfaces.label: Kiro CLI as an ACP agent (kiro-cli acp): spawned by an editor, by Kiro Crew, or as the engine child of an interactive session

Kiro CLI in a terminal (kiro-cli, kiro-cli chat; bun TUI plus kiro-cli-chat engine). One-shot listing and delete flags of `chat` (--list-sessions, --list-models, --delete-session) are excluded as whole tokens. Known cost of the whole-token deny-list: a session started with a prompt that contains a bare word such as `mcp`, `agent`, `login` or `help` is missed. `--no-interactive` runs are kept: they are working for their whole life

Kiro CLI.app in /Applications: signed wrapper that carries kiro-cli, kiro-cli-chat, kiro-cli-term and the menu-bar helper kiro_cli_desktop (LSUIElement). The helper is not a session, so no process rule

Kiro IDE (Electron, Code OSS fork). The bundled kiro.kiro-agent extension contains the agent's session server, so the agent is inferred to run inside the extension host with no per-session process; Kiro's docs call the harness 'a standalone process', so a child process is not ruled out and was not observed on macOS. The `kiro` shell shim runs Contents/MacOS/Kiro with ELECTRON_RUN_AS_NODE against Contents/Resources/app/out/cli.js for a moment; that short-lived process is excluded for the default /Applications path (macOS path inferred from the Linux shim)
Kiro Crew desktop app (Electron, open source). Runs a bundled Gateway and one kiro-cli acp child per agent session. Process rule inferred from electron-builder productName, never seen running
Kiro Crew Gateway (python -m kiro_crew gateway, dashboard on 127.0.0.1:5476). Process rule inferred from install docs (pipx or ~/.kiro/crew-venv), never seen running
Kiro Web (app.kiro.dev), Kiro Mobile (iOS TestFlight) and kiro-cli --cloud sessions: run in a managed cloud sandbox, nothing local to see

working_signals.meaning: Terminal sessions on the default V2 engine append to ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/<id>.jsonl (documented for ACP sessions; the interactive TUI drives the same engine over ACP, inferred; the session-management page instead says a per-directory SQLite database, so the docs conflict for interactive chats). Only resolvable when the process was started with --resume-id, because a fresh session has no id in argv. Raises working, never lowers it. Write cadence during a long model stream not measured. V3 engine and the IDE write ~/.kiro/sessions/<bucket>/sess_<id>/messages.jsonl instead (undocumented, read from bundled source), which this row's per_session path does not cover.

Weak fallback, unmeasured guess. Sums the whole tree under the matched process: bun TUI, kiro-cli-chat engine, MCP servers. The TUI redraws a braille spinner about 10 times a second while thinking (third-party report, kiro-cli 2.11), so a working turn should show CPU. It also over-reports: in kiro-cli 2.1.1 issue 7918 the engine was asleep with zero I/O after MCP failures while the bun TUI stayed in state R animating the spinner, so a hung turn still reads as working. A turn waiting on the network is not shown to be quiet; that is unmeasured

waiting_signals.meaning: The TUI writes this to its own terminal while a permission prompt or a question is pending. Same channel: OSC 9;4;3 while thinking or compacting, 9;4;2 on error, and while idle either 9;4;0 or, once context usage reaches 60 percent, 9;4;4;<context percent>. So state 4 alone does not mean waiting: only percent 100 does, and a full context window at idle also reads 100. Emitted only when TERM_PROGRAM is iTerm.app or WezTerm, WT_SESSION is set, HERDR_ENV=1 (Herdr, also true inside a tmux pane started by Herdr), or ConEmuANSI=ON (and not under tmux or screen for the ConEmu case); not for Terminal.app, Ghostty, kitty or cmux by that test. KIRO_NO_PROGRESS=1 turns it off. Readable only by the terminal host, never from ps. Docs (terminal-ui.md) confirm the feature and the iTerm2, WezTerm, Windows Terminal and ConEmu list but give no sequences. Sequences and conditions read from the bundled TUI source (functions mT, gCn, m1t, A1t; threshold constant mCn=60), re-read on the Linux arm64 2.25.0 build, not observed running

waiting_signals.method: BEL or OSC 9 (setting chat.notificationMethod: auto, bel, osc9)
waiting_signals.meaning: Text 'Permission required', 'Input required' and 'Response complete'. Off unless chat.enableNotifications is true. Docs list the settings; the message strings are from the bundled TUI source.

waiting_signals.method: macOS native notification from the IDE (Settings, Agent: Notifications)
waiting_signals.meaning: IDE only: 'Action Required' fires when the agent needs approval or input, 'Success' and 'Failure' at the end. No hook and no file; observable only as a Notification Center banner.
For an ACP client (an editor or Crew) that owns the stdio pipes: the agent asks for approval through this request. Not visible from outside the pipe.

hooks.config: CLI 3.0 and IDE 1.x: standalone JSON files, .kiro/hooks/*.json in the project and global hooks (~/.kiro/hooks/ per the IDE 1.0 page; the loader in the bundled agent has global hook directories). CLI 2.x (default engine): a hooks block inside the agent config, .kiro/agents/*.json or ~/.kiro/agents/*.json. Command hooks get JSON on stdin with session_id and cwd, and KIRO_SESSION_ID is set for shell commands (undocumented; found only as a string in the kiro-cli-chat binary).

telemetry.how: Kiro CLI only, undocumented: KIRO_TELEMETRY_OTEL, KIRO_TELEMETRY_OTLP_ENDPOINT and KIRO_TELEMETRY_EXPORT_INTERVAL_MS are read by the binary; it exports OTLP metrics (service kiro-cli, path /v1/metrics, e.g. kiro_cli_user_turn_duration_seconds), aggregates only, not a live turn signal. The documented OpenTelemetry export is an enterprise admin feature: daily kiro.daily.* metrics pushed from Kiro's servers at 02:00 UTC, not from the Mac.

sources.claim: Process tree of an interactive session (Linux, kiro-cli 2.1.1): `kiro-cli chat ...` launches `kiro-cli-chat chat ...`, which starts `bun tui.js chat ...` (the TUI) and `kiro-cli-chat acp ...` (the engine, talking ACP over pipes). The bun runtime and tui.js live in the data dir, ~/.local/share/kiro-cli/ on Linux.
sources.evidence: https://github.com/kirodotdev/Kiro/issues/7918 (process tree and per-process states) and https://github.com/aws/amazon-q-developer-cli/issues/3820 (crash banner: Args: "/home/kirouser/.local/share/kiro-cli/bun" "/home/kirouser/.local/share/kiro-cli/tui.js" "chat"). Linux only; macOS shape inferred.

sources.claim: The bun TUI, the node KAS server bundle and both runtimes are embedded in kiro-cli-chat and extracted on first run; env vars KIRO_AGENT_ENGINE, KIRO_KAS_NODE_PATH and KIRO_KAS_SERVER_PATH exist; 'Bun TUI runtime' and 'KAS agent engine' are named in launch.rs messages.

sources.claim: A turn writes a marker file <KIRO_TURN_MARKER_DIR>/<pid>-<startms>.json when it starts, refreshes last_alive_at_ms every 30 s, and deletes it when the turn ends. Keys: pid, engine, session_interface (interactive_cli), agent_mode, turn_started_at_ms, last_alive_at_ms, version_full, owner_started_at_s. The pid is the bun TUI process. A leftover file is reported by the host as an orphaned turn (metric kiro_cli_orphaned_turn_age_seconds). The directory is passed in by kiro-cli-chat; its path is not visible in strings (Rust names 'turn-markers' under a run dir chosen from XDG_RUNTIME_DIR or TMPDIR).
sources.evidence: Function IO(...) in the bun bundle extracted from kiro-cli-chat (const zbn="KIRO_TURN_MARKER_DIR", Kbn=30000, writes `${pid}-${startMs}.json`, unref'd setInterval, rmSync on end); Rust strings in kiro-cli-chat: 'crates/chat-cli/src/turn_marker.rs', 'struct TurnMarker with 8 elements', 'turn-markers', 'orphaned turn marker not removed', 'runtime directory not found: neither XDG_RUNTIME_DIR nor TMPDIR were found'. Undocumented. Never seen on disk. Re-read 2026-09-29 on the Linux aarch64 2.25.0 build (kiro-cli-chat strings: KIRO_TURN_MARKER_DIR, turn_marker.rs, turn-markers, kiro_cli_orphaned_turn_age_seconds; carved tui.js function IO matches the description).

sources.claim: V2 engine sessions (default) are saved every turn to ~/.kiro/sessions/cli/<session-id>.json (metadata) and .jsonl (event log), session ids are UUIDs, and a session can be active in one process only. The docs also say 'SQLite database in ~/.kiro/' for chat sessions, which contradicts the file layout.
sources.evidence: https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/acp.md (section Session storage) and https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/chat/session-management.md (Technical details: Storage SQLite database, Troubleshooting: Session is active in another process (PID XXXXX)); tui.js: `KIRO_TEST_SESSIONS_DIR??ja("sessions","cli")`

sources.claim: V3 engine and the IDE store sessions as ~/.kiro/sessions/<bucket>/sess_<id>/{session.json,messages.jsonl,sub-executions/*.jsonl}; bucket is '_global' or the first 16 hex of a sha256 of the workspace path. Not documented (the docs only say ~/.kiro/sessions/). KIRO_HOME moves the whole tree.
sources.evidence: @kiro/agent 0.66.11 dist/server/acp-server.js: `this.sessionsPath=r.sessionsPath??join(homeDir,".kiro","sessions")`, `join(n,"messages.jsonl")`, `join(e,"session.json")`, `iwt="_global"`, `substring(0,16)` of sha256; same sessionsPath line and a prompt string 'Sessions persist to ~/.kiro/sessions/<workspaceHash>/sess_<sessionId>/messages.jsonl' in the IDE's kiro.kiro-agent dist/extension.js. https://kiro.dev/docs/cli/v3/new-features.md says 'Session data is stored in ~/.kiro/sessions/'; https://kiro.dev/docs/reference/settings.md documents KIRO_HOME.

sources.claim: Hooks are standalone .kiro/hooks/*.json files (version v1, PascalCase triggers) in CLI 3.0 and IDE 1.x; CLI 2.x uses camelCase events (agentSpawn, userPromptSubmit, preToolUse, postToolUse, stop) inside the agent config. The docs disagree on Stop: the hooks table and hook-types page say it fires when the agent finishes responding; the CLI 3.0 migration page says 'Session ends'. The agent's own hook prompt says 'Stop: When an agent exec[ution completes]'.

notes: One harness, several surfaces. Kiro says the IDE, CLI 3.0, web and mobile share one agent harness (@kiro/agent); the default terminal engine today is still V2 (Rust engine kiro-cli-chat acp), V3 is opt-in with --v3. Terminal session: the launcher `kiro-cli` starts `kiro-cli-chat chat`, which starts a bun process running tui.js and a `kiro-cli-chat acp` engine child (Linux tree from a third-party issue; macOS not observed). The matched process is the outermost kiro-cli, so direct-child signals cannot reach the engine's shell tools or MCP servers (two or more levels down: kiro-cli, kiro-cli-chat chat, kiro-cli-chat acp, then the tools; the tools' parent is inferred to be the engine): do not use tool_children or child_process on this row. The most precise turn signal found is undocumented: a marker file per running turn in KIRO_TURN_MARKER_DIR (see sources; the TUI writes it only when that variable is set, and whether kiro-cli-chat always sets it is not shown); the schema has no signal kind for it, so it is not in working_signals. A detector that can read that directory (the bun process gets its path in the environment) should prefer it, and count a marker only while its pid is alive, since a crash leaves it behind. Binary pinning: kiro-cli-chat may run from a per-session hardlink or APFS clone rather than its install path (KIRO_SKIP_BINARY_PINNING=1 disables it), and the app path 'Kiro CLI.app' has a space, so argv[0] can be split by a ps parser; the row therefore matches on the base name and never on the install path. One-shot runs (`kiro-cli chat --no-interactive`) are working for their whole life. In the IDE the agent runs in the extension host, one process for every chat, so IDE CPU or children cannot name a thread; use a 10 percent floor there and never as the only reason. Kiro Crew's per-session `kiro-cli acp` children match the ACP surface and are children of a Crew process, so a detector should attribute them to Crew rather than count an idle interactive session. Not confirmed on a live instance: everything here comes from vendor docs, the vendor's own binaries read statically, and third-party reports. Process rules, checked 2026-09-29 against the sample tree in issue 7918: the engine child `kiro-cli-chat acp` matches the ACP surface but has a parent that matches the terminal surface, so the probe keeps only the outer process; `kiro-cli crew gateway` is excluded from the terminal surface and Crew's own `kiro-cli acp` children have a Gateway parent only if the Gateway rule matches. `kiro-cli --cloud` is a local client of a cloud session and matches the terminal surface. The daemon rule misses a pipx home under 'Library/Application Support' (space splits argv[0]) and the Gateway bundled inside the desktop app. Unknown or undocumented subcommands (for example legacy Amazon Q ones) are not excluded and would show as brief idle sessions.
